about.title: Mountain View Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Two people died in traffic collisions on Mountain View streets in 2025, according to public records. Behind each of those counts is a family in Santa Clara County trying to figure out what comes next. A wrongful death claim will not undo that loss, but it can address the financial ground that shifted underneath you: funeral and burial expenses, the income and support the person would have provided, and the love, companionship and guidance that no ledger fully captures. In California, the right to bring this claim belongs first to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children; certain dependents and heirs may qualify after them. The deadline generally runs two years from the date of death, and it runs shorter when a public agency is involved, which matters on corridors like El Camino Real, Shoreline Boulevard, US-101 and SR-85 where responsibility can be layered. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on El Camino Real in Mountain View. Where do I start?
items.answer: Start by requesting the collision report from the responding agency and preserving anything you have, such as photos, medical bills and the death certificate. El Camino Real is one of the higher-volume corridors in Mountain View, and crashes there can involve private drivers, commercial vehicles or public roadway questions, each with different timelines. An independent attorney can review the report and tell you which deadlines apply to your situation.

items.question: Is a wrongful death case the same as the criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by the family to recover losses, while a criminal case is brought by the Santa Clara County District Attorney to address a violation of law. The two proceed separately, and a civil claim can move forward whether or not criminal charges are filed.

items.question: What losses can a California wrongful death claim actually cover?
items.answer: Recoverable losses generally include funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have contributed over their lifetime, and the loss of love, companionship, comfort and guidance. The specific amount depends on the facts of each family, and no attorney can promise a result. An independent attorney can walk you through how each category is documented and valued.
